text: Christopher Crowe (c. 1681 – 9 November 1749) was an English consul and landowner. In 1705, at the age of 24, he was appointed English Consul at Livorno, in the Grand Duchy of Tuscany. He was awarded a "lucrative" contract to supply the British Mediterranean fleet with wine and olive oil during the War of the Spanish Succession, from 1703 to 1711. Crowe also served as a prize agent for captured enemy merchant ships, acquired artworks on behalf of the English nobility, and became wealthy. In 1707, he purchased Woodford Hall, a large house and estate in Woodford, Essex, adjacent to Epping Forest, from Sir Richard Child. In 1715, he married Charlotte Lee, Lady Baltimore, who had previously been married to Benedict Leonard Calvert, 4th Baron Baltimore, and they had five children. In 1727, he sold Woodford Hall to William Hunt, having secured a private act of Parliament, known as Crowe's Estate Act 1727 (1 Geo. 2. St. 2. c. 8 Pr.), to authorize the sale.
